Voltage adjustment range of 0.95~1.05 pu testing Demonstrate stability in simulations of common fault Stable in a Must remain stable in the expected highest scenarios at the Wide Range of SCR condition and lowest SCR condition expected range 8 SCRs over the lifetime of the project of SCRs Building on the metric framework, the project conducted multiple rounds of electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulations to validate GFM behavior under representative operating scenarios. Preliminary studies focused on confirming characteristic GFM responses, such as grid-forming angle regulation, voltage stiffness, and current-limiting behavior, while identifying feasible tuning ranges for primary control parameters. These studies examined disturbances including voltage steps, frequency excursions, phase-angle shifts, and low short-circuit strength conditions. The results confirmed expected GFM performance and provided essential parameter bounds for subsequent plant-level tuning. Comprehensive EMT studies were then executed using generic hybrid-plant models that incorporated GFM BESS, GFM wind, GFL wind, and GFL solar. These simulations assessed interactions between different inverter technologies, with particular attention to multi-resource dynamics under stressed system conditions. The work demonstrated that GFM units, unlike GFL resources, maintained stable angle synchronism across a broader range of system strengths, reduced sensitivity to phase-angle disturbances, and provided damped frequency and voltage recovery Page 11 of 36 Award Number: DE-EE0010651 Recipient Name: Portland General Electric following severe events.
